data.description:
## Context

The disposable quiet-window rehearsal for `561e-e186-a902-461c` proved that the history strip preserves tree/commit/merge/pack invariants but violates the required authorship identity invariant. Pre-rewrite `verify-identity` reported 8728 verified and 18 key-not-valid-at-era over 9875 in-scope events. Post-rewrite, with the correctly mapped enforce-since boundary and identical scope, it reported 3133 verified and 5613 key-not-valid-at-era. The cause is compacted authorship-ledger entries retaining their pre-rewrite `position.commit_sha`; the verifier trusts every non-null stored SHA and re-resolves by position only when the stored SHA is null. A commit-history rewrite necessarily changes those SHAs while preserving each event position.

## Plan

- Add a real-Git regression that creates signed events, compacts them into a ledger with non-null commit SHAs, rewrites commit history without changing the ticket tree, and proves the current verifier misclassifies the authentic ledger entry at the new epoch.
- In the whole-store verifier, treat a ledger `commit_sha` as a cache: when the ledger carries a position, resolve that position against the current tickets history and prefer the current resolved commit; retain the recorded SHA only as the fail-closed fallback when the position cannot be resolved.
- Preserve live-event behavior, ledger wire format, event bytes, current tree, and the existing null-commit recovery behavior.
- Re-run the disposable pre/post identity comparison and require identical summary counts plus identical `(event_uuid, verdict, grandfathered)` multisets when `commit` is ignored.
- Land through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, and zero unresolved comments before the maintenance window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [code-verifiable] A compacted ledger entry with a non-null pre-rewrite commit SHA is verified against the commit resolved from its position in the current history.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] If current-history position resolution fails, the verifier retains the recorded ledger commit SHA as its fallback.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] Live-event commit resolution and classification are unchanged.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The authorship-ledger persisted schema and event bytes are unchanged.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] A real-Git history-rewrite regression preserves the signed event verdict after all commit SHAs change.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The full disposable pre/post identity summaries are identical after the fix.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The full disposable `(event_uuid, verdict, grandfathered)` multisets are identical when rewritten commit SHAs are ignored.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The Gerrit fix lands with both required positive votes and zero unresolved comments.

## Scope

`src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py` and focused unit/integration tests only. No ticket-store event rewrite, no schema migration, and no authoritative maintenance mutation.
data.title: Preserve authorship-era verdicts across tickets history rewrite
